topIssues.title: kona-node: safedb dashboard and alerts
topIssues.author: einar-oplabs
topIssues.body:
Part of #23473. Depends on the metrics from #23478.

## Scope

Make the kona-node safedb observable on the devnets where kona-node runs, and page when it is unhealthy. The implementation lands in the k8s repo (Grafana dashboards and alert rules), following the existing k8s alert conventions (`team=protocol` routes to the protocol on-call; P3 and below is informational).

Dashboard, on the kona-node dashboard:

- safedb tip L1 block against the node's current L1 head, so lag is visible at a glance;
- safedb tip L2 block against local-safe;
- write, retry and truncation rates;
- a table of recent reset-below-tip warnings.

Alerts:

- safedb tip lagging the L1 head by more than a channel timeout for longer than 15 minutes while derivation is otherwise progressing (a gap is forming);
- any reset-below-tip warning (the condition that produced the hole in ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#402);
- write retries exhausted (the node stops, so this is a crash alert with a specific cause).

Threshold choices and a one-paragraph runbook per alert go into the alert annotations.

## Done

- [ ] Dashboard panels merged and visible for every kona-node on the kona-node sequencer devnet (ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#283).
- [ ] The three alerts are merged, routed to protocol, and each has a runbook annotation.
- [ ] Each alert has fired at least once in a deliberate test (for example by stopping writes or restoring a stale snapshot) and the on-call received it.

topIssues.title: kona-node: validate admin unsafe payload block hashes
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
## Summary

`TestInvalidPayloadThroughCLP2P` is skipped on kona-node because Kona's `admin_postUnsafePayload` RPC accepts an envelope whose claimed block hash does not match its contents.

op-node recomputes the block hash at the RPC boundary and rejects a mismatch before relaying the payload. Kona currently queues every payload immediately, so the malformed envelope returns success and is only rejected asynchronously downstream.

## Required change

- Add block-hash verification for OP execution payload envelopes.
- Reject mismatched payloads synchronously from `admin_postUnsafePayload`.
- Remove the Kona skip from `TestInvalidPayloadThroughCLP2P`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Kona's admin RPC returns an error for a payload with a mismatched block hash.
- [ ] Valid payloads continue to be queued for processing.
- [ ] `TestInvalidPayloadThroughCLP2P` passes with kona-node/op-reth and op-node/op-reth.

## Related

- Parent inventory: ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#101

topIssues.title: kona-node: support Beacon endpoint resilience and headers
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
The audit identifies an operator configuration gap: op-node supports beacon request headers and fallback/archive endpoints, while standalone Kona exposes a single beacon URL and a slot-duration override without equivalent configuration.

Define and implement the required endpoint selection and header behavior so operators can recover from a primary beacon outage and retrieve historical blobs from an archive endpoint.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Document the supported primary, fallback, and archive endpoint selection behavior, including the conditions for switching endpoints.
- [ ] Expose and wire the required CLI/environment configuration and request headers through production provider construction.
- [ ] Apply a bounded request/failover policy and preserve missing-blob and temporary-error semantics.
- [ ] Avoid exposing configured header secrets in logs or error messages.
- [ ] Tests cover primary failure, fallback success/failure, historical blob retrieval, and headers on the intended endpoints.
- [ ] Record an end-to-end validation of the supported failover and archive paths and document operator configuration.

Beacon query encoding and the kona-host slot-duration override are separate work. Alt-DA support is explicitly out of scope for Kona.

Source audit: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/23545.

Parent tracker: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/49.

topIssues.title: kona-node: encode Beacon blob query parameters correctly
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
The audit identifies a Beacon API compatibility gap: encoding versioned_hashes as a single comma-separated value is rejected or misinterpreted by some beacon clients.

Encode the array as repeated versioned_hashes query parameters, deduplicating outbound hashes while preserving the requested blob sequence in the result.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Distinct hashes produce repeated versioned_hashes parameters.
- [ ] Duplicate hashes are sent once, and their returned blobs are reused at every requested position.
- [ ] The result preserves the original requested order and length.
- [ ] A missing required blob remains an explicit error.
- [ ] Provider tests assert the exact outbound query and duplicate/missing-blob behavior; record validation against real beacon endpoints affected by the old encoding.

Implementation PR: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22594 (currently stacked on #22553). Endpoint failover, archive selection, and headers are a separate issue.

Source audit: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/23545.

Parent tracker: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/49.

topIssues.title: kona-node: support raw L1 receipt fetching with fallback
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
The audit identifies an L1 provider compatibility gap: Kona historical derivation can stall on eth_getBlockReceipts while op-node continues through debug_getRawReceipts on the same endpoint.

Support raw L1 receipt fetching with a standard-method fallback and preserve correct retry and reorg handling.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Fetch and decode raw EIP-2718 receipts, falling back to eth_getBlockReceipts when the raw method fails.
- [ ] MethodNotFound disables the unsupported raw method for the provider lifetime, including provider clones.
- [ ] Distinguish a missing block from an existing empty block; reject an empty receipt response for a non-empty block.
- [ ] Missing blocks trigger the appropriate reorg/reset handling, while temporary provider failures remain retryable.
- [ ] Regression tests cover fallback, malformed receipts, empty responses, and missing blocks; record validation against a real L1 provider.

Implementation PR: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22553. Beacon query encoding is tracked separately.

Source audit: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/23545.

Parent tracker: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/49.

topPRs.title: op-reth,kona-node!: build derived payloads at forkchoiceUpdated
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Alternative: #23454 builds derived payloads in a payload service wrapper instead, with no reth changes.

op-reth only found out that a derived block's transactions were invalid in its asynchronous payload build, after `engine_forkchoiceUpdated` had already answered VALID. An invalid forced transaction was skipped, so op-reth built a block that the fault proof rejects. An invalid `0x7D` failed the build instead, so `engine_getPayload` returned an error, the rollup node retried the same attributes forever and the safe head stalled.

op-reth now builds the payload of `noTxPool` attributes that carry a non-deposit transaction exactly once inside `engine_forkchoiceUpdated`. It does so in `OpEngineApi` with op-reth's payload builder, whatever payload service the node runs, so op-reth-premium is covered too, and answers `-38003` when the transactions make the block invalid. op-node and kona-node (fixed here) then replace the block with a deposits-only one. Deposit-only `noTxPool` attributes still go to the payload service.

- `engine_getPayload` hands the executed block to the engine tree through a new reth hook, `PayloadBuilderHandle::publish_built_payload` (ethereum-optimism/reth#16), so `engine_newPayload` doesn't execute it a second time.
- Attributes reth rejects keep reth's exact response. A build that fails for a node-local reason (missing state, provider error, panic) is never `-38003`; it takes the payload-service path as before.
- A retried request joins the running build or gets the built payload, and forkchoice updates are handled one at a time, so a fallback can't overwrite a newer forkchoice.
- For derived attributes with an invalid transaction, `debug_executePayload` returns the witness up to that transaction, where the fault proof program stops, instead of the witness of a block without it.

Latency for 30M-gas blocks (release build, median of 9, FCU + getPayload + newPayload + FCU), before → after: ETH transfers 120 → 95 ms, SSTORE 14 → 24 ms, KECCAK256 165 → 159 ms, ecrecover 388 → 389 ms, all within run-to-run noise (±10–20 ms). An invalid block is rejected at FCU after executing up to the failing transaction.

Supersedes #23188, whose kona-node fix and acceptance test this carries. Compared with it and with an earlier private fix (optimism-private@ed9e4d8):

| | #23188 | ed9e4d8 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Where it checks | payload job generator, at job creation | `OpEngineValidator::validate_payload_attributes_against_header` | `OpEngineApi`, in `engine_forkchoiceUpdated` |
| Derived attributes covered | `0x7D` only | all with a non-deposit tx | all with a non-deposit tx (one-line switch to all `noTxPool`) |
| Executions per derived block | 1 | 2 (validate, then build) | 1 |
| op-reth-premium | not covered (own job generator) | covered | covered |
| Invalid forced tx skipped (fault-proof mismatch) | yes | fixed | fixed |
| kona-node fix + acceptance test | yes | no | yes |
| Upstream changes | none | none | reth hook (ethereum-optimism/reth#16) |
| Costs | blocks the payload service while building; copy of reth's payload service builder | double execution; breaking `Evm` parameter on `OpEngineValidator` | copies reth's attribute checks; FCU serialized by a lock |

**Before merge:** move the reth pin from the head of ethereum-optimism/reth#16 to its commit on `optimism`, and re-tag the stale `UPSTREAM-MIRROR` reth tags (`just mirrors stale`); the only reth change is the payload-service hook.

Review agents (Rust, Go, derivation-batch, security) ran; their findings are fixed except:
- Dismissed, to confirm: no timeout on a derived build that holds the forkchoice lock. Builds are bounded by the block gas limit, a stuck state provider stalls reth's engine tree as well, and a request the rollup node abandons releases the lock.
- Not changed here, as kona-node with op-geth already behaves so: before Holocene, kona-node retries a `-38003` for derived attributes instead of dropping them; kona-node and kona-client gate the deposits-only replacement on the L2 timestamp, op-node on the L1 origin's; a transient error while building the replacement is critical.

BREAKING CHANGE: op-reth answers `engine_forkchoiceUpdated` with `-38003` when the transactions of derived attributes make the block invalid. op-node handles this. kona-node needs the change in this PR, otherwise it retries and stalls the safe head, so upgrade both together. Rust callers of `OpEngineApi::new` must pass the provider, validator and `DerivedPayloads` it builds derived payloads with, and `OpEngineApiBuilder` requires the node's pool, provider and EVM to fit op-reth's payload builder.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5*

topPRs.title: op-reth,kona!: replace invalid SDM derived blocks with deposits-only
topPRs.author: nonsense
topPRs.body:
A malicious or buggy batcher posts a batch to L1 for block N whose 0x7D is invalid, for example a refund larger than the gas the refunded transaction actually used. Every node has to agree on what happens to such a block, and the fault proof already decides it: the block is replaced by a deposits-only block, which keeps only the L1 deposits, and the chain moves on.

On op-reth that replacement never happened:

1. The rollup node asks op-reth to build block N (`forkchoiceUpdated` with the batch's transactions).
2. op-reth answers "OK, building", and only discovers the bad 0x7D later, inside its background build.
3. When the rollup node asks for the result (`getPayload`), op-reth returns a generic "unknown payload" error.
4. That error looks like a temporary glitch, so op-node and kona-node retry the same block forever.

The safe head is stuck at N-1 on every op-reth-backed node, for as long as that bad batch is on L1.

---

With the PR: op-reth runs the block during `forkchoiceUpdated` and rejects it right there with "invalid attributes". Both rollup nodes already know that answer means "use deposits-only". It also fixes a kona-node bug that this exposed: after building the deposits-only block, kona-node retried the original block and rebuilt the replacement in an endless loop.

Related to https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/368. The root cause is not SDM-specific: op-reth checks any derived block only in the background build, so batches without a 0x7D (for example an undecodable or invalid transaction) still stall or diverge; that is tracked in https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/308 and https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/341. Trade-off: a derived block with a 0x7D is executed twice, at `forkchoiceUpdated` and in the payload job.

BREAKING CHANGE: `OpEngineValidator::new` takes the EVM config.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

topPRs.title: kona-node,kona-engine,kona-rpc!: enforce conductor publication and recovery contracts
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
Superseded by five smaller draft PRs, stacked in merge order. The stack preserves all runtime changes from this PR and adds focused boundary tests.

| Order | PR | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | #23574 | Engine canonicalization |
| 2 | #23575 | Commit before publication |
| 3 | #23576 | Local recovery override |
| 4 | #23577 | Expected unsafe-head validation |
| 5 | #23578 | Conductor-managed activation |

All local checks pass, including both shared conductor client variants. Hosted CI is tracked on the replacement PRs. The original branch remains available for comparison.

---

Original description:

Kona currently canonicalizes sequenced payloads before conductor commit and ignores commit failures, which can publish an uncommitted unsafe chain. Separate detached sealing from canonicalization: commit first, then require `VALID` engine import/forkchoice before updating the unsafe head or gossiping. Failed commits retry the build token; temporary import failures retain the exact committed envelope. Invalid or stale work is discarded. Stop settles accepted work and preserves retries while inactive.

Closes #23264 and #23266. Also implements the remaining conductor activation/RPC contracts from #21906: managed startup stopped, leader and exact-head activation checks, configured RPC deadlines, correct external override parameters, and a process-local recovery override. Shared Go acceptance tests cover follower commit rejection, local disaster recovery, and exact-head activation using the existing real-Kona fixture.

Targets `develop` independently. Includes the five-line reset-head publication correction also present in #23544, so activation sees initialized heads without requiring that PR. Selects the needed behavior from #23229, #23492, #23493, and #23486 without their prerequisite refactors. #23484 independently owns malformed admin payload validation; the umbrella conductor tickets #21903 and #21906 also depend on that work and runtime acceptance results.

Validation: all 323 affected Rust engine/RPC/service/binary tests, full workspace Rust lint, Go lint (zero issues), Go API compatibility, and independent Rust and Go/API reviews pass. Nextest reported one cleanup warning in an unchanged attributes test; its isolated cleanup check passed. The full shared conductor suite passes against op-node/op-reth (13 tests) and Kona/op-reth (12 tests, one expected malformed-payload skip owned by #23484). Hosted CI is green, including both real-client acceptance jobs. Local readiness requires `RUST_LOG=info`; the final Kona run used a temporary wake assertion after an earlier run crossed host sleep and large wall-clock jumps.

BREAKING CHANGE: `admin_startSequencer` now requires the expected unsafe-head hash, matching op-node. Rust integrators must supply that hash, implement `Conductor::leader` and separate `seal_block`/`canonicalize_block` methods on `SequencerEngineClient`, supply `conductor_rpc_timeout` in `SequencerConfig` literals, and handle the new canonicalization task/request/error variants. The unused `SequencerAdminAPIError::LeaderOverrideError` variant is removed.

topPRs.title: kona-node!: commit sequenced payloads before publication
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
Kona currently imports sequenced blocks before conductor acceptance and continues publishing after rejected commits. Require acceptance before validated import or gossip, retain the build token for failed commits and the exact accepted envelope for temporary import failures, and settle accepted work when stopping. Configured RPC deadlines bound conductor waits.

BREAKING CHANGE: Rust implementers must replace `seal_and_canonicalize_block` with fetch-only `seal_block`; `SequencerConfig` literals must supply `conductor_rpc_timeout` (one second by default). Downstream exhaustive matches must also handle `ConductorError::Timeout` and `SequencerActorError::ConductorCommit`. Related: #23264, #23266.

Part 2/5 replacing #23547. Merge in order: #23574 → **#23575** → #23576 → #23577 → #23578. Review against the immediate parent; PR 1 targets `develop`.

Validation: 330 affected Rust tests and full workspace Rust lint pass. Go lint reports zero issues; the shared conductor acceptance package compiles. Rust, Go, and API/deletion reviews completed. Aggregate runtime behavior matches #23547 on current `develop`; extra changes are focused tests and sealing rustdoc.

Hosted CI is green.
